steps.text: Preheat an oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C).

Mix flour, sugar, salt, baking powder, and baking soda together in a large bowl. Stir in brown sugar, oats, and chocolate chips. In a separate bowl, combine oil and vanilla extract; stir into flour mixture. Press dough into a 15x10 inch jelly roll pan.
Bake in the preheated oven until lightly brown, about 15 minutes. Cool before cutting into bars.

raw_recipe.headline: Vegan Davy Crockett Bars
raw_recipe.description: A vegan version of the popular oatmeal and chocolate chip cookie bar.
raw_recipe.name: Vegan Davy Crockett Bars

recipeInstructions.text: Preheat an oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C).

Mix flour, sugar, salt, baking powder, and baking soda together in a large bowl. Stir in brown sugar, oats, and chocolate chips. In a separate bowl, combine oil and vanilla extract; stir into flour mixture. Press dough into a 15x10 inch jelly roll pan.
Bake in the preheated oven until lightly brown, about 15 minutes. Cool before cutting into bars.

review.reviewBody: I reduce both sugars by 1/4 cup. Added 1/2 cup of applesauce to the oil and vanilla because the other reviews convinced me to add some moisture. The applesauce keeps it vegan, unlike the egg that another review suggested. Pushed the dough into prepared 9x13 glass baking dish. Baked 350 for 30 minutes. I just ate a piece and it is delicious, still warm. I think they will cool and cut well. My version is thicker more like an oatmeal chocolate chip cookie bar. I use vegan chocolate chips from Whole Foods and they taste just the same as regular. This recipe is similar to the cowboy cookie mix in a jar recipe that I made from this site.

These were very close to the "non-vegan" recipe submitted by Kimberly32. I don't usually read all of the reviews on recipes, I probably should though. I made these tonight, and when I poured in my oil into the dry, even after mixing, it almost resembled a crisp topping w/ chocolate chips and the chocolate chip cookie mixes you get in the bag. So I went to read on the reviews about what to do & a common theme was reducing sugars and oils and using 1/4- 1/2 c applesauce. So I added 1/2 c applesauce, & it still seemed a little dry to me, but I put it in the pan anyway and hoped it would turn out. I added the regular 3/4 c oil, and 1/2 c applesauce. I also reduced the sugars down to 1/2 c each. Next time I plan on 1/4 c oil to 1/2 c applesauce and just 1/4 c of each of the sugars. This was a good recipe! When my mom found out it was vegan, she was apprehensive. After they baked and cooled she ate one, and then determined they weren't bad after all. So thanks so much for this recipe!

I followed the recommendations to reduce amounts of both sugars by 1/4 cup and add 1/2 cup unsweetened applesauce. I also added about 1/4 cup vanilla almond milk because I still didn't think there was enough liquid, a little extra vanilla, and 1/3 cup chopped pecans for crunch. Baked at 350 for 27 minutes and the texture was excellent. Slightly crusty on top, soft and gooey elsewhere. Sweetness was perfect for serving as a snack, after school to kids for example, but if I wanted to serve as a dessert I'd add back the omitted sugars. A great recipe to tailor according to your taste and purpose.

This is a great base recipe, but I cut down on the sweetener and eliminated the white sugar like most of the people below. I also added barley, ground flax, and almonds for a little more crunch and a little more protein. Came out very tasty!

These were SO GOOD!!! At our Xmas cookie party, my Crockett bars were super popular, even though they were the only vegan offering! Following the advice of another reviewer, I cut each kind of sugar by 1/4 cup and added 1/2 cup of applesauce. I also subbed raw sugar for white sugar, of course, to make it vegan. Instead of chocolate chips, I used dried apricots and walnuts. I will definitely be making this one again!

I read some reviews and followed the suggestions as follows: cut back on all Sugars by 1/4 cup and add 1/2 cup Apple Sauce. Also I made my brown sugar from scratch because I didn't have any. I used 1 cup white sugar and 3 TBSPNS of King Syrup (molasses is recommended if you have but I didn't). King Syrup is thick as Honey and is the only syrup I'd recommend for the replacement of Molasses, for its a Golden Syrup that has a light Molasses taste. Lastly as a result they came out GOOWEY AND CHEWY!

I took the advice I found in previous reviews to cut the sugar by a quarter cup and add a half cup of applesauce. The dessert came out perfectly itwas very gooey (a bit messy to eat but who cares?!!?) and my non-vegan skeptic friends even had to agree. It was a hit!

I halved this and made it as cookies, with a few changes as follows: (* indicates a modification) 1 c. flour *3/4 c. vegan sugar 1/2 tsp. salt 1/2 tsp baking powder 1/2 tsp. baking soda 1 c. oats 1/2 c. vegan chocolate chips 1/2 tsp. vanilla *1/2 c. applesauce *2 TBSP. vegetable oil *2 TBSP. rice/soy milk. They came out a little cakey, but still pretty good cookies for no egg.

I just made this and it is delicious but I do agree with others that there is way too much sugar. I reduced each sugar by 1/8-1/4 C. but next time I will use 1/2 C. white sugar and 3/4 C. brown. I also pureed 2 ripe bananas and added them at the end. The banana flavor is delicious and it makes it very moist but they don't seem to cook on the bottom. Next time I might try only 1 banana. Either way - yum!

These were delicious! The only change I made was to add 1/4 C applesauce. My daughter with milk/egg allergies gobbled them up - as did our non-vegan friends! No one would have guessed they were allergy friendly!
Very very crumbly, needs more liquid to make it more like a bar. Was not chewy or gooey. I love the applesauce idea and will try again with the applsauce added instead of sugar.

YUM! I have a dairy/lactose intolerance and it's really hard for me to find a cookie that I can eat AND enjoy! They were super easy to throw together and next time I make them, I may use a little less sugar - also, maybe around Christmas I'll add some cinnamon and dried cranberries! Thanks :)

There definitely has to be more moisture in these, as well as a healthier version. The reader that cut the sugar and added apple sauce is right on, as well as cutting some of the processed sugar for agave, or another version of a lower glym index sweet. FYI, I don't know where they get the recipes on this site, but most vegans don't use white sugar, based on being processed through a method of bone char, using animal bones.
Mine were not chewy or gooey. Very very crumbly but the flavor was good.
The cookies came out dry and crumbly. They tasted alright but they weren't chewy and gooey like I was hoping for.

We made two dozen and ours weren't chewy or gooey, but they were simply delicious! Depending on your taste, you may want to reduce the amount of sugar in the recipe, they were very sweet. Next time we make them, we're not going to use as much sugar. Enjoy!
